output.question: What is fuboTV's short interest?
output.answer: In the latest FINRA settlement (October 30, 2026), 6,838,404 FuboTV (NYSE: FUBO) shares were sold short. That is up 7,577 shares from October 15 (6,830,827) and represents about 6.42 days to cover. Stockanalysis.com shows roughly 6.83M shares short, which it puts at about 22.8% of the float (about 29.94M shares) and 6.26% of all shares outstanding (109.20M). Short interest has risen steadily since mid-September, when it was 6.22M shares. Share counts from before March 24, 2026 can't be compared directly, because FUBO did a 1-for-12 reverse split that day; for example, about 61M shares were short in late 2025 on the old basis.

key_facts.fact: FUBO short interest was 6,838,404 shares at the 2026-10-30 settlement, up 7,577 from the prior report, with 6.42 days to cover on average daily volume of 1,065,625.

Stockanalysis.com shows 6.83M shares short (prior month 6.22M): 22.82% of float, 6.26% of shares outstanding, and a short ratio of 5.62 days. It lists float at 29.94M and total shares outstanding at 109.20M.
FUBO did a 1-for-12 reverse stock split on March 24, 2026.

passages.quote: Shares Short 6.83M (prior month 6.22M); Short % of Shares Out 6.26%; Short % of Float 22.82%; Short Ratio 5.62

caveats: Sources disagree on the percent of float. Stockanalysis puts it at about 22.8% using a float of 29.94M shares, which appears to be the publicly traded Class A float after the Disney/Hulu Live combination. Against all 109.20M shares outstanding it is only about 6.3%. Other sites list roughly 23–25% of float.
Stockanalysis's 6.83M figure has no settlement date. It matches both the Oct 15 and Oct 30 FINRA figures, so it is unclear which one it reflects.
The next FINRA settlement (2026-11-13) has not been published yet, so these numbers may change soon.
Share counts from before March 24, 2026 (for example, about 61M short in late 2025) are on the pre-split basis and can't be compared with current figures without adjusting for the 1-for-12 split.
These figures are from third-party aggregators; I could not open FINRA's primary data directly.
